replacementSteps: Safely raise vehicle and support with jack stands
Remove five lug nuts (84-114 ft-lb torque)
Remove wheel and inspect brake components
Clean wheel hub and bearing face
Install new or refurbished wheel, hand-tighten lugs
Torque lugs in star pattern to 84-114 ft-lb
Retighten at 500 miles after wheel work
parts.mentorScript: Front left wheel removal and installation. Always use jack stands and never work under a vehicle supported only by a hydraulic jack. OG torque is 84 to 114 foot-pounds. After any wheel disturbance, retighten lug nuts at 500 miles.

replacementSteps: Locate lug nut on wheel hub (five per wheel)
Using 3/4" socket and torque wrench
Tighten to specification: 84-114 ft-lb (113-153 N·m)
Use a star or cross pattern to ensure even load
Do not over-torque; can strip threads
Retighten all lug nuts at 500 miles after any wheel work
Check annually for looseness with torque wrench
parts.mentorScript: Wheel lug nuts secure the wheel to the hub. The 2004 OG specification is 1/2 inch by 20 threads per inch, torqued to between 84 and 114 foot-pounds. Use a torque wrench in a star pattern. Over-torquing can strip the hub and wheel studs. Always retighten at 500 miles after any wheel disturbance.
